newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTO HOPE FOR MIRACLE AGAINST UNITED.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTO HOPE FOR MIRACLE AGAINST UNITED.

text.p: Porto go into Wednesday's European Cup quarter-final second-leg tie against Manchester United knowing only a miracle can keep them in the competition.
After a humiliating 4-0 defeat at Old Trafford in the first leg two weeks ago, the odds against the former European champions scoring the five goals they need to survive are huge.

Not only are Manchester United currently on top form in the English league, while Porto have been beaten in two of their last three domestic games, the home side have lost a number of key players to injury and suspension.
"Practically impossible," was how coach Antonio Oliveira described the task facing his "dragons", the nickname for the Portuguese champions.

Neverthless, Oliveira promised that his side, European Champions 10 years ago, would not go out without a fight. "We are not going to throw in the towel. We are going to try and put right everything that went wrong two weeks ago," he said.
But Porto will be without bustling Brazilian striker Artur Oliveira, midfielder Rui Barros and defender Sergio Conceicao -- all suspended after picking up yellow cards in the first leg.
International striker Domingos Oliveira and winger Antonio Folha are sidelined through injury.
United have no such problems as they bid to become the first English side to reach the semi-finals of Europe's top club competition since 1985.
The only doubt for coach Alex Ferguson surrounds the fitness of striker Andy Cole who limped out of his side's 2-0 defeat of Sheffield Wednesday at the weekend with a thigh strain.
If Cole fails to recover, he is likely to be replaced by Nicky Butt in a slightly more defensive formation with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer taking the main striker role.

Both defender Gary Neville, who needed stitches in an ankle injury sustained against Wednesday, and midfielder Ryan Giggs, who hurt a knee in the same match, are expected to be fit. United can also call on influential midfielder Roy Keane who missed the first leg through injury.
Probably the only thing the Portuguese have going for them is history. The last time these two teams met in the European Cup in 1977 Porto won 6-5 on aggregate.
But the chances of history repeating itself are slim to say the least.
Porto - Henrique Hilario, Jorge Costa, Aloisio Alves, Fernando Mendes, Paulinho Santos, Jose Barroso, Edmilson Pimenta, Zlatko Zahovic, Ljubimko Drulovic, Mario Jardel, Grzegorz Mielcarski.
Manchester United - Peter Schmeichel, Gary Neville, David May, Gary Pallister, Denis Irwin, David Beckham, Roy Keane, Ryan Giggs, Eric Cantona, Nicky Butt, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.
